meta.title: The potential adverse effects of hypodermic glucagon-like peptide -1 receptor agonist on patients with type 2 diabetes: A population-based study.
meta.abstract:
Background

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), a class of injectable antidiabetic drugs, have shown significant efficacies in improving glycemic and weight control in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the long-term safety of GLP-1 RAs remains insufficiently studied. This study aimed to provide real-world evidence on potential adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use in T2D patients without major chronic diseases including impaired cardiac or renal function.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 7746 T2D patients on GLP-1 RAs in Shenzhen, China. They were compared with 124 371 metformin-only users and 36 146 insulin-only users, forming two therapy control groups. GLP-1 RAs users were also further 1:2 paired with the control groups. Competing risk survival analyses were conducted to assess the incidence risks, presenting subdistributional hazard ratios (sHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for various adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use.

Results

Compared with metformin-only users, GLP-1 RAs use was associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes (sHRs with 95% CIs), including pancreatitis (2.01, 1.24-3.24), acute nephritis (3.20, 2.17-4.70), kidney failure (3.73, 2.74-5.08), thyroid cancer (2.25, 1.23-4.10), and thyroid dysfunction (1.27, 1.00-1.63), respectively; Similar results were also found when compared with insulin-only users. Importantly, long-term (≥12 months) GLP-1 RAs use may further elevate the incidence risks of pancreatitis, acute nephritis, thyroid cancer, and thyroid dysfunction.

Conclusion

Compared with traditional T2D treatments, GLP-1 RAs use may be associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes in a Chinese population. Cautions were strongly warranted in the use of GLP-1 RAs. Further validation is crucial across diverse populations.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: Metformin monotherapy users represent early/mild T2D whereas GLP-1 RA users had higher baseline obesity (BMI 25-39.9: 43.72% in GLP-1 vs 34.37% in metformin in Table 3S) and higher socioeconomic status (undergraduate+: 26.07% vs 11.94%; citizen health insurance: 75.60% vs 54.96%). Critical clinical confounders such as diabetes duration, baseline eGFR, microvascular complications, and glycemic control (HbA1c missing in 90.52%-91.79%) were unmeasured or unadjusted, pushing risk estimates away from the null.

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Surveillance and diagnostic workup bias strongly favors detecting thyroid nodules/cancer, acute nephritis, and pancreatitis in patients receiving newer, heavily monitored, self-injected GLP-1 RAs compared to routine metformin users.

findings.title: Surveillance bias and differential diagnostic intensity
findings.mechanism: Patients prescribed novel, expensive GLP-1 RAs (which carry specific label warnings for pancreatitis and thyroid C-cell tumors) undergo increased diagnostic imaging, laboratory tests, and specialist visits compared to patients on standard oral metformin.
evidence: Table 2S: Outcomes identified via ICD-10 and regular expression matching on clinical notes (e.g., thyroid cancer C73/C75, pancreatitis K85/K86, acute nephritis N00-N08)
Reported sHR of 15.09 (95% CI: 4.65–48.98) for leukemia in long-term GLP-1 RAs vs metformin strongly suggests diagnostic scrutiny differences or severe residual confounding

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Multiple outcomes and post-hoc duration cutoffs were tested across multiple comparator cohorts without an established pre-registered protocol, increasing the likelihood of selective reporting of positive associations.

findings.title: Multiple testing across multiple clinical categories without pre-registration
findings.mechanism: A wide battery of ICD-10 disease categories across six organ systems was scanned across multiple drugs and duration thresholds without multiplicity adjustments.
evidence: Section 2.2 lists six organ systems evaluated across 4 individual GLP-1 RA agents and 2 duration strata without citation of a pre-published statistical analysis protocol

overall.summary: This retrospective electronic health record cohort study is at very high risk of bias, primarily driven by severe confounding by indication, extreme missing data (>90% missing baseline HbA1c and ~33% missing BMI), surveillance/detection bias for known label warnings, and participant selection. Propensity score matching failed to address these issues because 'unspecified' missing status was treated as a matching category, leaving substantial residual imbalance. The extreme effect estimates (e.g., sHR 15.09 for leukemia, sHR 3.73 for kidney failure vs metformin) contradict established trial evidence and reflect substantial bias away from the null.

unresolvable_without_more_data: Raw event counts for each adverse outcome in the matched and unmatched cohorts (only subdistribution hazard ratios and demographic numbers were reported in the text and tables)

baseline_comparability.summary: GLP-1 RA users were younger but had substantially higher baseline rates of overweight and obesity, alongside greater health insurance coverage and higher educational attainment. These baseline imbalances, compounded by >90% missingness in HbA1c and unmeasured diabetes duration, likely biased risk estimates for adverse outcomes away from the null.
